cards.explanation: The man is begging for his son. He says, “Lord, have mercy on my son…” so his begging is for his boy. He gets down on his knees and asks for mercy, and nothing in his words is for himself. I think a dad who kneels in front of a crowd has already stopped caring who's watching. Then he tells Jesus what his son is going through.

The answer is False. The man tells Jesus, “I brought him to Your disciples, but they could not heal him.” So he brought his son to the disciples first, and they could not heal him. Now he is the one kneeling in front of Jesus.

The answer is that Jesus says to bring the boy to Him. He says, “Bring the boy here to Me.” Right after some strong words, the next thing out of His mouth is a way forward for the boy. He doesn't send the dad off or tell him to come back later. He asks for the boy to be brought right to Him.

The answer is the demon. The text says, “Then Jesus rebuked the demon, and it came out of the boy…” The demon is what Jesus speaks to, and it leaves. The boy was healed from that moment. A rebuke from Jesus is all it took.

The answer is False, friends. After Jesus rebuked the demon, it came out of the boy, and “…he was healed from that moment.” There are no days of waiting and no slow recovery in the text. It happens at once.

The disciples ask Jesus, “Why couldn’t we drive it out?” They came to Jesus privately to ask it. They had tried to heal the boy and could not. I think they had a hard question on their minds, and they took it to the right person.

The answer is faith. Jesus says, “Because you have so little faith…” That's the reason He gives, and I'm not adding one of my own. Then He goes right into talking about a mustard seed. Faith is the whole topic here.

Jesus compares faith to a mustard seed. He says, “…if you have faith the size of a mustard seed, you can say to this mountain, ‘Move from here to there,’ and it will move.” He talks about faith by its size, and He picks a seed. Then He adds, “Nothing will be impossible for you.” Every word of that is what He says.

The answer is True. Jesus says, “Nothing will be impossible for you.” He says it right after talking about faith the size of a mustard seed. Those are His exact words to His disciples, and they come with the mountain moving from here to there. It's the last thing He says in this part.

The answer is that they will kill Him. Jesus says, “They will kill Him…” This is a heavy one, and I think it was hard for the disciples to hear. He is saying it about Himself, since the Son of Man is the name He uses for Himself (Mark 2:10).

The answer is True. Jesus says, “…on the third day He will be raised to life.” He says it right after telling them He will be killed. So the heavy news and the promise are in the same breath. Those are His words, and they stand together.

The answer is grieved. The text says, “And the disciples were deeply grieved.” Jesus had just told them He would be killed. I think anybody would be grieved to hear that about someone they follow. It's sad news, and the text doesn't hide that.

The collectors ask whether Jesus pays the two drachmas. They say to Peter, one of Jesus' disciples, “Does your Teacher pay the two drachmas?” They bring the question to Peter, but it's about his Teacher. Peter is the one who gets asked. Jesus is the one the question is about.
The answer is True. When the collectors ask if his Teacher pays the two drachmas, Peter answers, “Yes.” After that, Peter enters the house, and Jesus speaks to him first.

Peter answers, “From others.” Jesus had asked whether the kings of the earth collect customs and taxes from their own sons or from others. Peter gives the second one. Then Jesus says, “Then the sons are exempt…”

The answer is False, friends. After Peter says, “From others,” Jesus tells him, “Then the sons are exempt…” So the sons don't pay. Jesus still sends Peter to the sea, though, and He says so that they may not offend them.

Jesus says Peter will find a four-drachma coin. He tells Peter that when he opens the mouth of the first fish he catches, he will find “…a four-drachma coin.” Then Jesus says, “Take it and give it to them for My tax and yours.” A coin is exactly what Jesus names.
The answer is False. Jesus tells Peter, “Take it and give it to them for My tax and yours.” The coin covers Jesus' tax and Peter's. It's one coin for the two of them.
